Hi Rajesh / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of goals:
- Integrate Redwood inference into Acme's analytics pipeline for real-time scoring and embeddings-based search.
- Keep traffic on private network where possible; minimize public egress for PII-regulated workloads.
- Support both text generation (tool-calling/structured outputs) and embeddings+reranker flow for search ranking.

Items we covered and immediate asks:
1) Networking: you prefer no public-egress for requests containing sensitive data. You asked about VPC endpoints, IP allowlists, DNS behavior, and mTLS.
2) SDK/auth: you wanted recommended auth approaches for hosted vs private deployment (API keys vs mutual TLS / short-lived tokens).
3) Routing & model pinning: confirm ability to route to specific region/variant and fallbacks.
4) Embeddings/reranker: expected throughput and batching recommendations.

Proposed next steps:
- Dev (cc'd) to provide a short checklist (networking endpoints, sample firewall rules, DNS guidance) and sample SDK auth snippets.
- Acme to share a high-level network diagram (private subnet, NAT/Egress, DNS) and confirm which workloads require strict private-only connectivity.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (30–45m). We suggested Tue 2026-06-16 10:00 PT — does that work?

Attachments: redwood_vpc_integration_guide.pdf (integration guide), networking-checklist.xlsx (initial checklist).

Marissa — thanks for the recap. A few clarifying questions from our infra/security team so we can prepare the diagram and decide whether we need Dedicated/Private: 

1) Hosted vs Private connectivity model:
- For the hosted API, can we avoid public egress from our private subnet? In GCP we'd prefer Private Service Connect or VPC egress rules so traffic never goes over the public internet.
- If we use Redwood Dedicated or Private, do you support VPC peering, Private Service Connect (GCP), or AWS PrivateLink?

2) IP allowlist & stable egress IPs:
- Do you provide stable egress IP ranges we can allowlist on our firewall / WAF? Are those per-region or per-customer?

3) mTLS / client certs:
- Is mutual TLS supported for authentication to Redwood endpoints (hosted)? If not, is there a short-lived token approach tied to KMS or a proxy? We have strict mutual-auth requirements for some endpoints.

4) DNS & SNI behavior:
- If we use a VPC endpoint, how is DNS resolved? Will we need to add CNAMEs in our private DNS? Any special SNI constraints for routing?

5) Embeddings/reranker throughput:
- For our use-case we'll run high-QPS embedding lookups and a cross-encoder reranker for top-50 results. Do you have recommended batching/replication configuration or throughput numbers to size Dedicated capacity?

6) Structured output / tool calling:
- When using the SDK's tool-calling/structured output, does the request payload go to the same endpoint as regular generation? Any added latency or special routing considerations?

If you can get Dev to provide a short network checklist and sample SDK auth snippets, that would help our network team prepare. We'll also attach a draft network diagram in the next email.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Director of Platform Engineering | Acme Analytics

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singing@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & SDK integration next steps

Hi Rajesh / Priya —

Thanks for the questions — below are pragmatic answers and what we recommend for each item. I’ve attached a short checklist (networking-checklist.xlsx) and the integration guide. If you can share the network diagram we’ll mark it up.

1) Hosted vs Private connectivity model
- Hosted (fastest onboarding): We support private connectivity via cloud-provider private endpoints in many regions (AWS PrivateLink and GCP Private Service Connect) for customers that want private egress to Redwood without opening public internet paths. This is a per-customer configuration that routes traffic over provider private networks to our ingress.
- Dedicated/Private: For customers who need full data-plane isolation, we offer Dedicated pools and a Private deployment option. Those support VPC peering and direct cross-connects in select regions. Recommend Private for regulated workloads where you cannot allow any public egress.

2) IP allowlist & stable egress IPs
- We can provide stable egress IP ranges for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted private endpoints, allowlisting is done at the endpoint level and is per-customer-per-region.
- If you need explicit IP ranges for firewall rules, we can supply the prefixes for the region after we know the deployment mode (hosted-private-endpoint vs dedicated).

3) mTLS / client certs
- Mutual TLS is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated endpoints with customer-managed certs.
- For Hosted API we primarily authenticate using API Keys (short-lived tokens supported via our OAuth token exchange for automation). If you require mTLS equivalent for Hosted, we can work with our networking team to evaluate a customer-specific PrivateLink + client-cert option, but the standard Hosted path uses TLS with API-key/short-lived-token authentication.

4) DNS & SNI behavior
- For provider private endpoints, we generally provide a FQDN that you map in your private DNS (we provide the CNAME/alias). SNI is standard; ensure proxies preserve SNI for routing to the correct tenant endpoint.
- If you use an egress NAT + allowlist, DNS resolution happens locally and outgoing HTTPS goes to our public hostname (not recommended for private-only requirements).

5) Embeddings/reranker throughput
- Recommended pattern: compute dense embeddings in batches (batch size tuned to your latency profile) and store in your vector DB. For reranking, we recommend a two-stage approach: (1) fast ANN nearest-neighbor with embeddings to surface ~100 candidates, (2) cross-encoder reranker (higher cost) to re-rank top candidates.
- For sizing Dedicated capacity: provide expected QPS for embeddings and QPS for reranker calls (top-K rerank requests). As a rule of thumb, embedding calls can be batched heavily to reduce cost; rerankers have lower batching tolerance because of latency requirements. We can share model-specific throughput numbers after we know which model family you prefer.

6) Structured output / tool calling
- Tool calling and structured output use the same endpoint/service as text generation. The additional work is on the SDK side to pass a function schema and process returned structured JSON. No special network routing is required; however, tool-calling can increase request/response size (and sometimes callouts to your tool endpoints) — if your tool endpoints are internal, ensure they are reachable from the environment executing the handlers.

Quick SDK auth examples (hosted):
- API Key (server-to-server):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer rwd_live_XXXX" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"gpt-qa-1","input":"..."}'

- Short-lived token exchange (recommended for automation):
  1) Your service mints a short-lived JWT and calls our token-exchange endpoint with a customer API key bound to your project.
  2) Our token-exchange returns a short-lived inference token (15m) that you use in the Authorization header for calls from ephemeral compute.

mTLS (private): if you deploy Private we’ll provide the client cert bundle and instructions:
  curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://private-api.redwood.local/v1/generate -d '...'

Network checklist (high-level) — what we need from Acme to proceed:
- Target deployment mode: Hosted-private-endpoint vs Dedicated vs Private
- Region(s) and preferred cloud provider (GCP/AWS)
- Private DNS plan (will you add CNAMEs/aliases?)
- Egress model (NAT with allowlist OR Private Service Connect / PrivateLink)
- Any mutual TLS requirement or cert mgmt preferences
- Estimated QPS for embeddings and reranker calls + acceptable p99 latency

Action items:
- Please share the network diagram you mentioned. We’ll annotate and return recommended firewall rules and the per-endpoint DNS records.
- Marissa will coordinate a 30–45m technical deep-dive next week.

Thanks — happy to jump on the call to walk through a sample VPC setup.

Best,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
